title: Spinal cord anatomy: grey matter, tracts and roots
description: Cross-section: a grey butterfly inside white tracts, wrapped in three meninges.

questions.question: Where does the spinal cord end in adults?
questions.answer: The spinal cord usually tapers to the conus medullaris near the L1-L2 vertebral level in adults; nerve roots continue below it as the cauda equina.

questions.question: What is the difference between gray and white matter in the spinal cord?
questions.answer: Central gray matter contains neuronal cell bodies and local circuits; surrounding white matter carries ascending sensory and descending motor pathways.

questions.question: What is the posterior (dorsal) horn?
questions.answer: The slender upper horns receiving sensory afferents; laminae I–VI including the substantia gelatinosa. Function: First synapse for pain, temperature and touch; gate control of nociception happens here.

questions.question: Where is the lateral horn located?
questions.answer: Present only in T1–L2, holding preganglionic sympathetic neurons (and S2–S4 parasympathetic equivalents). Function: Origin of the sympathetic outflow.

questions.question: What is the function of the white funiculi & tracts?
questions.answer: Function: Highways for sensation upward and motor commands downward. Dorsal columns (fasciculus gracilis & cuneatus), lateral spinothalamic and corticospinal tracts, and spinocerebellar tracts.
